categories.distinction: Evidence bootstrap and QA gating as first-class triage steps
categories.rationale: Recurs across all three artifact classes. Operates on metadata, not structural measurements. Already the dominant practical signal in every tested inventory. Representation-agnostic by design.

categories.distinction: Conservative candidate narrowing (broad input to narrow output)
categories.rationale: Workflow shape survives representation change in all three classes. The narrowing logic is the same everywhere: QA first, task boundaries second, structural risk third.

Confirmed in LoRA and checkpoint delta. Not testable in LoHa (same-task only panel). Guardrail: state that cross-artifact task-relation ordering is observed where testable but not exhaustively validated across all representation forms.
Confirmed in LoRA and checkpoint delta. The three-way ordering holds where testable. Guardrail: same-family behavior depends on the task-family registry, which is still small (sentiment_binary, NLI).

categories.distinction: Triage as the cross-artifact decision scenario
categories.rationale: Only triage has complete coverage across LoRA, LoHa, and checkpoint delta. Safe to describe triage as a broader workflow. Guardrail: do not imply merge or routing work across artifact classes.
Well-validated in LoRA but not observed in LoHa or checkpoint delta. May be a panel coverage gap rather than a real limitation, but cannot be claimed as cross-artifact until confirmed elsewhere.

categories.distinction: Factor-geometry-specific structural cues (subspace overlap, V-module ratio)
categories.rationale: Representation-locked to factorized artifacts. Cannot be computed from checkpoint summary representation. The strongest sidecar signal but not portable.

categories.distinction: Merge strategy recommendations across artifact classes
categories.rationale: Merge execution is operationally restricted to native LoRA. LoHa merge is unvalidated. Checkpoint delta merge is out of scope. Do not surface strategy strings for non-LoRA artifacts.

categories.distinction: Numeric compatibility scores as cross-artifact comparisons
categories.rationale: Scores exist in all classes but use different scales. LoRA same-task 0.475 vs checkpoint delta same-task 0.892 are not comparable. Ordinal ranking may transfer; absolute values do not.
Unique to checkpoint delta Representation C. No analog in factor-based pipeline. Product-facing descriptions should not reference summary-profile-specific comparison metrics.

categories.distinction: Pair risk labels as cross-artifact comparison
categories.rationale: Same vocabulary (low/medium/high) but different calibration per representation family. LoHa same-task 'low' and checkpoint delta same-task 'medium' do not mean the same thing.

summary.bottom_line: The cross-artifact substrate is real but narrow. It consists of workflow-level signals (evidence gating, narrowing) and task-relational ordering, not structural metrics. Product language can safely reference the workflow shape and evidence-gating pattern across artifact classes. It should not reference structural measurements, numeric scores, or merge strategies as cross-artifact primitives.
